clue.text: Greedy man swallowing with passion turned to topping

indicators.note: a greedy eater swallowing something takes it inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: a greedy person is called a pig

indicators.note: turned means the short pieces for with and passion are read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger, a fierce passion

explanation.surface: A glutton gobbling something that has, in a fit of temper, turned into a dessert topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' suggests a dessert garnish but means something worn on top of the head; 'turned' reverses the two short pieces (giving ERIW) and 'swallowing' encloses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A periwig is a powdered wig of the kind once worn by gentlemen, so a topping for the head.

clue.text: One floored having constant interruption ‹ his?

definitions.text: One floored having constant interruption ‹ his?

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into something, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: a plank is a board laid as flooring
C is the usual symbol for a constant in physics and maths

explanation.surface: Someone knocked down and kept being interrupted wonders whose fault that was.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the physicist Max Planck gave his name to Planck's constant, so 'constant ... his?' points to him. The odd mark before 'his' stands for a dash in the dataset text.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Planck, the German physicist, gave his name to the fundamental quantum constant h.

clue.text: Noted pier needed repair, so tackled the brickwork

indicators.note: something needing repair must be put back together, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A seaside pier in poor shape was mended by a mason who redid its brickwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed repair' rearranges the nine letters of NOTED PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Repointing is renewing the mortar between bricks, a job on brickwork.

clue.text: Overcoming resistance, Dickensian club member gives tip

indicators.note: read as coming over, the outer word comes over and around the smaller piece, holding it inside

parts.note: Nathaniel Winkle is a member of the Pickwick Club in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A character from Dickens's club, having got past opposition, passes on a piece of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Winkle is one of the Pickwick Club's members in Dickens's first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrinkle is an informal word for a clever trick or useful hint.

clue.text: Drop in church attendance

parts.note: reads as falling numbers at services, but means dropping to one knee when in church

explanation.surface: Fewer people are going to church these days.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests declining congregations; the real sense is a worshipper bending the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: To genuflect is to bend the knee in reverence, as Catholics do before the altar.

clue.text: Beginning to rain, standing around under this?

definitions.text: Beginning to rain, standing around under this?

indicators.note: one piece standing around another encloses it, so the first letter of rain goes inside

parts.note: standing in the sense of rank or position is status

indicators.note: the beginning of the word rain is its first letter

explanation.surface: Rain is just starting, and people stand about beneath grey cloud wondering if it will pour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts R, from 'Beginning to rain', inside STATUS; the whole clue pictures the low grey cloud that brings drizzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is low, flat, grey cloud that often gives drizzle.

clue.text: Eratosthenes' invention used by the Jumblies

definitions.meaning: the Greek mathematician's method for finding prime numbers by striking out multiples
in Edward Lear's nonsense poem the Jumblies went to sea in a leaky vessel full of holes

explanation.walkthrough: The Jumblies are Edward Lear's nonsense characters, who famously 'went to sea in a Sieve'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sieve of Eratosthenes is an ancient prime-finding method, and Lear's Jumblies sailed in a sieve as their boat.

clue.text: Animal showed sign of injury and didn't walk straight

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
bleeding is a sign that one has been hurt

explanation.surface: A hurt beast was bleeding and staggering about.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramble is to wander aimlessly rather than heading somewhere directly.

clue.text: Sign "for you, Grahame"

parts.note: for in the sense of addressed to: a gift for or to someone
Kenneth Grahame, author of The Wind in the Willows, addressed by his first name, shortened

explanation.surface: A dedication on a card made out to the author Grahame.
explanation.walkthrough: A gift label 'to Ken' is one 'for you, Grahame', Kenneth Grahame being the author of The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a symbol or indication of something, as in a token of thanks.

clue.text: Ending is certain to include resolution of case

indicators.note: one word including another holds it inside

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: the resolution of something works it out afresh, so the letters of case are reordered

explanation.surface: Closing a matter is bound to involve settling the case in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending' looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition, in its noun sense of a stop; 'resolution of' reorders the four letters (CEAS) and 'to include' holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: Surcease is an old word for a cessation or stop.

clue.text: Two pages to replace one line in description of nato equipment

indicators.note: one thing put in to replace another is swapped in where the other stood

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance
L is the abbreviation for line
P is page, so two of them are PP

explanation.surface: Two sheets of paper are swapped in for a line in an account of NATO's hardware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' swaps one L of ALLIANCE for PP.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or piece of apparatus, so an item of equipment.

clue.text: One's dying to meet him

parts.note: sounds like eagerness, but refers to the idiom of meeting the creator when one dies

explanation.surface: Someone is desperate to be introduced to a certain man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dying to meet' suggests eagerness; literally, the dead go to meet their Maker, God the creator.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet one's Maker is to die, Maker being God as creator.

clue.text: Kind of beetle, to come down on mouse

definitions.meaning: a beetle that springs into the air with a snapping sound when on its back
pressing a finger down on a computer mouse button

explanation.surface: A beetle pounces on a mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a predator and its prey; the 'mouse' is the computer kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The click beetle is named for its snapping jump, and pressing a mouse button is a click.

clue.text: Fish in the country, not regularly employed

indicators.note: the fish is placed in the country, inside its name

parts.note: France is a country
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone fishing in the countryside who has no steady job.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works for several clients on contract rather than holding a permanent post.

clue.text: Those sweets very cheap, I understand

definitions.meaning: read literally: the boiled sweets called drops cost one penny
an idiom for finally grasping something

explanation.walkthrough: Drops are small boiled sweets, so a phrase about penny-priced drops doubles as the idiom for sudden understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: When the penny drops, comprehension dawns, from coins dropping in a slot machine; read literally, drops priced at a penny.

clue.text: Citizens' earnings I redistributed

definitions.note: the possessive is dropped: the definition stands for the plural citizens

indicators.note: wealth redistributed is spread out differently, so these letters are shared out in a new order

explanation.surface: A tax policy that hands out the people's income to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redistributed' rearranges EARNINGS I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigerians are nationals of Nigeria, its citizens.

clue.text: Being compliant in showing medal, not gold, in interview

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour with a medal

indicators.note: not marks something to be left out, here the symbol for gold

parts.note: an audience is a formal interview, as with the Pope or monarch
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone shows deference by wearing an honour, not a gold one, at a formal meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes AU from AUDIENCE, leaving DIENCE. The OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is doing as one is told, the state of complying with orders.

clue.text: Gas Newton compressed expanded again

parts.note: Newton shrinks to its symbol, one letter; spelling that same letter out in full a different way gives a gas

explanation.surface: Gas that has been compressed and then allowed to expand again.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the symbol for the newton; expanded again, the same N is the chemical symbol of a gas, so the clue asks what else N stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the colourless gas with chemical symbol N, making up most of the air.

clue.text: Again be lifted, bursting with no end of energy

definitions.text: Again be lifted, bursting with no end of energy

indicators.note: something bursting flies apart, so the letters of the opening phrase scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tireless leaps up again and again, overflowing with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursting' rearranges AGAIN BE LIFTED; the whole clue pictures someone with endless energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefatigable means tireless, never running out of stamina.

clue.text: Running: not leading, and not second or third

indicators.note: not marks the letters in second and third place of the word as left out

parts.note: something not in the lead is following behind

explanation.surface: Runners in a race: one not in front, and not in second or third place either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not second or third' removes the second and third letters, O and L, of FOLLOWING.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowing means running, as water runs in a stream.

clue.text: Stand, having good time, in rowdy place

parts.note: to bear something is to stand or tolerate it
pi, short for pious, means good in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone at a rough venue puts up with it and still enjoys themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is a crossword convention for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear pit was a pit for baiting bears, and the term now means a scene of noisy confrontation.

clue.text: One deceiving wife gets support

parts.note: an easel is a stand that supports a painting

explanation.surface: A cheating husband whose wife nevertheless stands by him.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person, by figurative extension from the animal.

clue.text: Sky feature, to run hello sailor? The opposite

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the opposite of a hello is a goodbye, adios; a sailor is a tar

explanation.surface: Something seen in the heavens; a jaunty greeting to a seaman, but reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' turns hello into its opposite, ADIOS (Spanish goodbye), so 'goodbye sailor' is ADIOS + TAR, after R for run.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio star is a celestial object that emits strong radio waves, an astronomical source in the sky.

clue.text: Amid sound of battle, soldier must prepare trench

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the soldier goes inside

parts.note: din is the loud noise of fighting
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Amid the noise of combat a soldier has to dig a defensive trench.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in is to excavate a defensive position, entrenching oneself.

clue.text: Working hard to send up new satellite

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up reads it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: hard at it means working hard

explanation.surface: Scientists toil to launch a new satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to send up' reverses AT IT to TITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn, a natural satellite.

clue.text: By start of evening Christmas tree may be lit up

indicators.note: by means next to, so the first letter of evening sits beside the tree

parts.note: a Christmas tree may be a fir

indicators.note: the start of evening is its first letter

explanation.surface: By the time evening comes the Christmas tree may be illuminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' sets E, the 'start of evening', next to A FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire means on fire or burning, so alight.

clue.text: Singer's performance with relish, from the heart

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a gig is a musical performance

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so the central letters of relish

explanation.surface: A singer performs with gusto and genuine feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Beniamino Gigli was a celebrated Italian operatic tenor; 'from the heart' takes LI, the middle of RELISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniamino Gigli was a famous Italian tenor of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Ringing sounds on carriage harness

definitions.note: a singular noun for what the plural answer names: the decorated harness of a horse

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a trap is a light two-wheeled horse carriage
pings are short ringing noises

explanation.surface: Bells jingle on a horse-drawn carriage's harness.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the ornamental coverings and gear of a horse, its decorative harness.

clue.text: Figure twelve carp may be caught

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so one piece is trapped within the other

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock
to carp is to nag or complain

explanation.surface: Anglers hope to land a dozen carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like a fish and 'twelve' a count; they are NAG and NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a geometric shape with nine sides.

clue.text: Edith, don't slump!

definitions.meaning: the English poet Edith, known for her striking upright appearance
a command to keep good posture in the chair

explanation.walkthrough: Edith Sitwell was a 20th-century English poet; read as two words, the answer is an order to sit up properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edith Sitwell was the poet, and telling someone to sit well means to keep good posture.
